messages:
Priya: Heads-up team — today were releasing the FIPS KMS opt-in for Private deployments. This is an opt-in change (no tenant is switched without action) and includes a migration helper to rotate legacy keys into the FIPS module. Runbook + migration CLI: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-fips-optin
Jon: Nice. Any billing or perf implications we should tell customers about?
Priya: Minimal perf impact. Key ops (rotate/decrypt metadata) may add ~1-3ms on first access due to the FIPS provider handshake; weve instrumented this. No billing changes for storage; KMS request counts will appear under "security.kms_requests" telemetry.
Maya: Ops note: migration helper will create a temporary key version and replay a safe rotation. If you want to test on a dev tenant, use the sample below:
```
# preview migration plan (no changes)
redwoodctl private fips-migrate --tenant acme-dev --preview true

# run migration with scheduled window (UTC)
redwoodctl private fips-migrate --tenant acme-dev --window "2026-04-15T02:00:00Z" --notify customers
```
Priya: InfraBot will run canaries against 5 dev tenants tonight. InfraBot: canary scheduled at 02:00 UTC, health-check cadence 30s.
InfraBot: canary-start -> group: dev-canaries-5; metrics stream: https://metrics.redwood.internal/dashboards/fips-canary
Jon: Who owns the customer comms for opt-in vs mandatory? I assume Legal + SE?
Legal: Correct. We need a short guidance note for customers that explains opt-in benefits, expected timings, and the mandatory enforcement plan for legacy keys in 30 days if they don't opt. Draft shared: https://redwood.internal/notice-drafts/fips-optin-comm
SE-Team: We'll batch-contact customers flagged as high-risk (finance, healthcare). SEs: please add any tenants that require hands-on migration in the shared spreadsheet.
Maya: Rollback plan: if we detect >0.5% key-op error rate or >5s median key latency for 10m, the canary aborts and we automatically revert newly created key versions. This is instrumented in the rollout controller.
Priya: Action items: 1) Eng: watch canary dashboard and set alerts for rollback thresholds. 2) SEs: review draft customer note and tag accounts needing migration. 3) Legal: finalize notice for 7-day pre-enforcement warning. 4) Ops: confirm maintenance windows for enterprise customers.
Jon: One more ask 94 can we add a non-FIPS verification token so customers can assert theyve completed migration for audits?
Priya: Yes — we added a "fips_migration_verification" field in the audit bundle. It includes key_versions rotated timestamp + operator id. Example in runbook.
InfraBot: staged-rollout started for private-fips-optin v1.0 -> canary group; status: in-progress; logs: https://deploys.redwood.internal/logs/rollout/4271001111
Priya: Summary: feature is live as opt-in today, canaries running tonight. Mandatory legacy-key enforcement scheduled in 30 days; customers will receive a 7-day notice before enforcement. Please review the runbook and file any concerns here. :white_check_mark:
